title: Make Loci relationship retrieval effective in ordinary agent work
outcome: Establish how agents discover, select, and consume Loci relationship capabilities in ordinary repository tasks; carry the evidence-backed decisions, agreed corrections, actual-host delivery, and outcome verification through the same Objective. Judge success by correct source-backed answers and retrieval cost, with explicit uncertainty, rather than graph-call counts alone.
details: Vik requested an adoption investigation after a Claude run made no graph calls, endorsed a fresh-context diagnostic, and on 14 September 2026 confirmed that Manifest carries both Planning and Implementation. This Objective therefore extends beyond the audit: preserve the completed diagnostic, finish the scoped evidence, agree warranted changes, implement the selected work, and verify it in actual agent workflows. Vik explicitly authorized switching this same Objective to Implementation on 14 September 2026 after decomposition review and reaffirmed that direction after clarifying the legacy decomposition flag. Execute the decomposed audit and its necessary bounded tooling under this authorization; no repeat phase or audit-tooling approval is needed. Evidence-backed product corrections remain selected through the existing finding-disposition tasks. Initial evidence: docs/reviews/2026-09-14-graph-adoption-audit.md. A fresh Terra/high agent used 13 shell commands, no Loci calls, and no deferred discovery; its post-task discovery exposed all 21 Loci tools. Historical records also contain real relationship deliveries. Production stats cannot attribute graph/explore use. One diagnostic does not establish frequency, causality, or broad benefit. Preserve the completed exploration Objective as separate prior work. No access to Vik's private work repository is needed. Selected corrections may belong in product telemetry/tool contracts, host discovery, installed operating instructions, or other source justified by evidence. Capture unresolved decisions explicitly and retain negative or inconclusive findings.

tasks.title: Select ordinary cases and independent answer evidence
tasks.outcome: Define a small workload that can distinguish useful relationship retrieval from legitimate direct reads.
tasks.details: Candidate accessible repositories: Anvil, llm-wiki and Loci, selected by real task shape and supported language relationships. Include same-named declarations or cross-module contracts/impact and a direct-symbol or unsupported-relationship control. Decide the smallest language/repository coverage needed for the intended claim, rather than a full model-language matrix. Freeze source snapshots; keep expected identities, required answer facts and negative cases evaluator-only. Formats must express the task naturally, without arbitrary hidden JSON or path-spelling traps. A candidate starting workload is four task shapes: cross-file dependency, incoming impact/callers, imported/type contract, and a direct-read control. The freeze task chooses and justifies the final count.
completionCriteria: Every selected case has ordinary user wording, fixed source identity, independently verified answer facts and explicit uncertainty/negative expectations.

tasks.outcome: Specify a trustworthy observation contract and the smallest capture route that can satisfy it.
tasks.details: Choose reusable host traces, corrected benchmark adapters, a thin boundary observer or production events using a documented comparison. Record actual executed operations and returned outcomes; handle nested Code Mode calls, loops, dynamic dispatch, shell fallback, failures and truncated results without counting text mentions. Classify graph record/traversal tools, explore intent, get type-context opt-in, actual relationship counts and source bytes. Tool delivery alone cannot establish hidden reasoning or causal answer use. Select retention, attribution and readout needs proportional to the audit. Treat graph anchors/health and containment-only neighbors separately from semantic relationship delivery; record actual edge family and counts rather than trusting a graph-prefixed name. Define answer support only through observable final claims tied to delivered proof; do not infer internal cognition.

tasks.title: Define host strata and matched retrieval conditions
tasks.outcome: Separate natural adoption from deliberate diagnostics while matching the conditions needed for each claim.
tasks.details: Cover Rowan's primary workflow as well as delegated fresh-context behavior. Pin selected model/reasoning settings, host, actual reachable catalog, skill/ambient instructions, source and store configuration. Verify actual account/runtime availability for selected settings; do not infer support from an advertised schema. For the initial ordinary condition, do not prime agents with graph hints or prior failures. Declare any visibility-only or task-shaped routing intervention separately and reuse one schedule across discovery and utility analyses. Claude's inaccessible private work environment is outside scope; no cross-host claim without host evidence. A small repeated case block is preferred to a full matrix. Two repeats before/after per selected case is a candidate, not an approved run count or population estimate; retain a meaningful primary-role check rather than substituting only delegated Terra behavior for Rowan.
completionCriteria: Every condition has an explicit question, available runtime and delivered instruction/tool surface, with intentional differences separated from uncontrolled ones.

Adapt only the minimal audit-specific observer/scorer needed by the selected contract, with isolated stores and deterministic fixtures. This is an audit prerequisite, separate from a later decision to add product telemetry. Implementation is authorized from 14 September 2026, including the bounded audit-adapter prerequisite when existing capture is insufficient. Record the chosen adapter scope and evidence, then execute it without asking again for phase or audit-tooling permission. Broader product measurement remains a later evidence-backed selection.

tasks.title: Measure tool visibility and retrieval choices
tasks.outcome: Establish where agents lose the route from available tools to relationship retrieval.
tasks.details: Use one frozen execution schedule for both discovery and usefulness. First retain the actual as-delivered catalog/instructions without priming the ordinary task agent, then collect declared runs and diagnose route choices. An instructed ALL_TOOLS-first condition is a separate intervention, never silently inserted into the natural baseline.
completionCriteria: Every scheduled discovery/routing observation is retained, including failures and non-use, with actual visibility evidence.
Findings distinguish tool availability, discovery, instruction routing and justified fallback; their scope and unresolved causes are explicit.

tasks.title: Inventory actual discovery and instruction delivery
tasks.outcome: Establish what each selected host and agent role actually receives before interpreting its choices.
tasks.details: Record main-agent and subagent capability catalogs, deferred discovery access, emitted bootstrap text and installed skill provenance. Trace the owned source to its installed copy and loaded host. Include Codex Code Mode and any other host explicitly selected in the freeze. A sidecar or separate capability probe must not inject extra hints into the natural task agent. Targets include skills/loci, README bootstrap guidance, configured loci-mcp launcher and relevant Anvil host adapters; inspect owner paths before deciding edits.
completionCriteria: Each selected environment has an as-delivered tool/instruction receipt and source/install provenance, with absent or unverified surfaces explicit.
Availability checks are distinguished from agent-initiated discovery and from any post-task prompt that changes behavior.

tasks.title: Execute the shared ordinary and diagnostic schedule
tasks.outcome: Collect the frozen runs once for both routing and usefulness analysis.
tasks.details: Run exactly the declared conditions with fresh context and fixed source inputs. Initial ordinary prompts contain no graph hints. Retain native calls/results, shell fallback, answer, elapsed time and available provider usage. Keep diagnostic interventions separately labeled. Record tool visibility and instruction identities for each run; do not substitute a standalone client as proof of the actual host.
completionCriteria: Every scheduled attempt has an immutable outcome or explicit incomplete/failure record, and all declared channels/costs are captured.
No selective replacement, outcome-driven prompt change or extra campaign is hidden in the baseline; untouched continuation obeys the freeze.

tasks.title: Locate discovery and selection failures
tasks.outcome: Explain observed routing breaks at the boundary supported by evidence.
tasks.details: Use the shared runs to distinguish unavailable tool, skipped deferred discovery, stale/missing instructions, schema misunderstanding, appropriate exact-read choice and unsupported relationship. Compare natural versus declared diagnostic conditions only as permitted by the design. Do not generalize one Terra failure to all models or infer that instructions alone repair it.
completionCriteria: Every claimed routing failure links the task, delivered surface, observed choice and evidence; legitimate non-graph work is separately accounted for.
Findings name the smallest confirmed owning boundary and preserve unresolved competing explanations without claiming unsupported causality.

tasks.title: Assess relationship consumption and task value
tasks.outcome: Determine whether delivered graph evidence is consumed and where it affects correctness or retrieval effort.
tasks.details: Separate case-specific graph capability from what agents invoke, what gets delivered, observable final-answer support, and total task cost. Independently inspect supported source identities and omission boundaries. Reuse the shared runs; do not collect a second overlapping baseline or infer hidden cognition from packet delivery.
completionCriteria: Scheduled traces identify delivered relationships, omissions, follow-up retrieval and supported answer use.
Correctness and retrieval-cost findings include all agreed runs and limits, permitting a negative or inconclusive result.

tasks.title: Check case-specific graph opportunity and delivery limits
tasks.outcome: Establish whether the frozen source graph can supply relationship evidence useful to each case.
tasks.details: Use controlled evaluator-side probes against the fixed snapshots after case truth exists. Validate exact identities/proof lines and supported semantic subsets; inspect partial/unresolved/omitted paths and output budgets. Keep this diagnostic separate from ordinary adoption. Recheck current compact graph-reference/call defaults before carrying forward the private report's oversized-response observation; already-delivered fixes are not new implementation requirements.
completionCriteria: Each case distinguishes proven available relationships, unavailable/unsupported relationships and delivery omissions using exact source identity.
Probe requests, returned source/proof and limits are retained; no new graph engine defect or repair is inferred solely from absent ordinary calls.

tasks.title: Assess proof delivery, answer use and total cost
tasks.outcome: Measure what the shared runs delivered and whether their answers used that evidence.
tasks.details: Replay the shared traces, correlate requests/results, classify graph-bearing explore/get/explicit graph operations, and assess answers against independent source truth. Count exact reads and deliberate hydration as real workflow cost without labeling every follow-up a failure. Cite observable answer/evidence use where present; mark internal consumption unknown where it cannot be observed. Include all errors, helpers, retries and fallbacks.
completionCriteria: Each run has verifiable delivery/cost accounting or an explicit missing-data state, with repeated and unique source delivery kept distinct where measured.
Answer correctness, identity ambiguity, uncertainty and observable proof use are assessed independently of invocation count; measurement failures cannot become zero-use or zero-cost observations.

tasks.title: Synthesize practical value and remaining uncertainty
tasks.outcome: Determine which capabilities help the sampled tasks and which failure classes warrant action.
tasks.details: Combine matched comparisons with graph-opportunity checks. Separate discovery loss, inappropriate routing, source/proof omission, unsupported semantics, answer mistakes despite correct context, and useful non-graph navigation. Report costs and outcomes at the task/condition level. Preserve historical rejections and avoid claiming benefit from a successful diagnostic packet alone.
completionCriteria: The report states supported benefits, regressions, negative and inconclusive findings with the declared denominators and retained failures.
Each proposed follow-up is tied to a specific task/result and ownership boundary; no general adoption or efficiency claim exceeds the workload and runtime evidence.

tasks.title: Agree finding dispositions and concrete corrections
tasks.outcome: Select warranted changes and their delivery surfaces before implementation.
tasks.details: Reconcile every finding with its owner, previous fixes and concrete delivery proposal. Agree selected implementation, explicitly disposition unselected candidates, and update remaining required leaves/dependencies in this same Objective. A graph-engine repair requires a demonstrated defect and added scoped delivery work. Implementation direction is already recorded from 14 September 2026. Use this task to choose concrete warranted corrections and preserve the existing audit authority, not to request the phase transition again.
completionCriteria: Each required finding has an evidence-backed fix, accepted no-change/defer decision, or explicit unresolved decision.
Selected work identifies affected source and installed/runtime surfaces, acceptance checks, and Implementation direction; its required delivery is represented in this graph.

tasks.title: Disposition findings and propose owned corrections

tasks.details: For each finding, identify the owned code, tool contract, installed instructions or host configuration; record candidate/no-change/defer status and rationale. Compare improving discoverability with changing retrieval routing, and existing observation with product telemetry. Propose a graph-engine/output change only for a demonstrated remaining defect; if selected, add specifically scoped delivery leaves here before implementation. Keep unrelated improvements separate.
completionCriteria: Every finding has a cited disposition and named owner/delivery surface; overlapping and already-delivered fixes are reconciled.
Each proposed correction has a concrete before/after behavior, smallest relevant acceptance check and expected task value.

Retain the existing authorization for bounded audit-support implementation; product corrections still require their concrete selection.
completionCriteria: The selected changes and acceptance boundaries are recorded against their graph Tasks, with unselected candidates explicitly dispositioned.
Required implementation and actual-host verification are represented in this same Objective and the phase reflects Vik's actual direction.

completionCriteria: All selected discovery/routing/product corrections are implemented on their agreed source and installed delivery surfaces, or individually resolved by accepted no-change decisions.
Focused checks cover the observed failure scenarios and preserve justified non-graph retrieval, unsupported/partial results and exact-source requirements.

tasks.outcome: Measure the selected changes with fresh context on the agreed task workload.
tasks.details: Use the predeclared post-fix conditions and fixed task snapshots, matching provider/host/model settings where possible. Count all scheduled outcomes, failures and retrieval costs. Include legitimate direct-read/control tasks as well as relationship-heavy work. Primary and delegated behavior remain separate. A graph call does not rescue an incorrect answer, and correct source delivery does not prove the agent reasoned correctly.
completionCriteria: Every planned post-change attempt is retained and accounted for under the frozen rules, with actual-host provenance and no selective replacements.
Correctness, evidence use and workflow cost meet the selected acceptance criteria or yield an explicit negative/inconclusive disposition; changes to uncontrolled conditions are disclosed.

tasks.title: Publish the adoption verdict and close required follow-through
tasks.outcome: Finish with an inspectable ordinary-use view and an evidence-bounded decision on the improvement.
tasks.details: Reconcile the entire recursive graph to Vik's accepted outcome, retained audit, selected changes and actual-host/task evidence. Publish the readout location and practical supported use cases/limits. Establish acceptance or remaining required work explicitly; a finished audit or successful activation does not establish routine adoption. Record durable operating changes and leave optional future ideas separately dispositioned.
completionCriteria: All required selected changes have source, actual-host and relevant task acceptance evidence; unresolved required outcomes keep the Objective open.

Vik can inspect the scoped usage/readout and benefit findings, including failures and accepted negative/no-change outcomes; the stopping decision follows the agreed outcome rather than task-count completion.
